newsitem.title: GERMANY: HDI says to take San Paolo stake, buy unit.
newsitem.headline: HDI says to take San Paolo stake, buy unit.

text.p: German insurance group HDI said on Thursday it is to take a one percent stake in Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino SpA and acquire its BNC insurance unit.
HDI, led by mutual Haftpflichtverband der Deutschen Industrie VVaG, said it has undertaken to acquire one percent of the Italian bank in its present privatisation.
It added that it is paying 250 billion Lira for 70 percent of Italian insurer BNC Assicurazioni. San Paolo is retaining the remaining 30 percent.
"This is the basis for a wide-ranging co-operation in the Italian insurance market," said HDI chief executive Wolf-Dieter Baumgartl.
BNC achieved in 1996 premium volume of 217.0 million marks, HDI said. Of that, 84.5 million marks were life premiums and 132.5 million marks non-life, mainly motor.
BNC was originally part of a foundation run by the Italian railways, which had banking and insurance interests.

In 1992, the banking side was transferred to Banca Nazionale delle Communicazioni SpA, the insurance activities to BNC Assicurazioni. Both were taken over in 1994 by Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino.
